title: How I used AI to build a Road Rash-inspired racer
author: trollmania1
selftext:
I made Desi Mayhem, a free Road Rash-inspired browser racer set across six Indian cities.

I started with a motorcycle combat game for Indian roads. I built it in Three.js and WebGL, used Blender and Blender MCP for model work, and used Image Gen for the title-art workflow. I called it Desi Mayhem.

Chennai came first. The first playable build made me want to keep going, so I spent the next two days building with Astra. I kept adding details I recognise from the road: local buses, auto stands, roadside shops, and traffic that blocks the line you want to take.

Mumbai needed BEST buses and a wet seafront. Bangalore needed flyovers and green-and-yellow autos. Patna needed Gandhi Maidan. I built each route around familiar streets, vehicles, landmarks, and traffic patterns.

The first rider models looked like stretched circles stacked together. Astra helped build vehicles including buses and the Tata Ace. I also brought in existing 3D models for stronger riders and more convincing traffic, adapted them for the game, and credited their creators.  


I kept refining the riding, crashes, and controls, then added races against seven rivals. Now I can race through streets I recognise, squeeze past an auto, and get knocked off my bike for trying.

Playable build: [https://desimayhem.com](https://desimayhem.com)

I’m happy to answer questions about the Image Gen, Blender MCP, or Three.js/WebGL workflow.
